question: Using the definition of ADS and Table 5A-1, explain why Level 2 is not an ADS level while Level 3 is.
model_answer: Direct Answer: An Automated Driving System (ADS) is defined as hardware and software capable of performing the *entire* Dynamic Driving Task (DDT) on a sustained basis, a term reserved for Level 3, 4, or 5 systems. Level 2 does not qualify because, although it executes both steering and acceleration/deceleration, the human driver is still expected to perform "all remaining aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task" — so the system performs only part of the DDT and is categorized as ADAS. Level 3 qualifies because the system performs "all aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task within a given ODD," with the human driver serving only as a fallback who responds to a request to intervene. Standards (mandatory): - The acronym meanings are mandatory: "ADS-Automated Driving System" and "ADAS-Advanced Driver Assistance Systems" are among the acronyms that "when used in this Manual, shall have the following meanings." Support (informational): - "Automated Driving System (ADS) – The hardware and software that are collectively capable of performing the entire Dynamic Driving Task (DDT) on a sustained basis, regardless of whether it is limited to a specific Operational Design Domain (ODD); this term is used specifically to describe a Level 3, 4, or 5 driving automation system." - Per Table 5A-1, Level 2 is "the driving mode specific execution by one or more sustained driver assistance systems of both steering and acceleration/deceleration … with the expectation that the human driver performs all remaining aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task," and its Automation Category is "Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)." - Per Table 5A-1, Level 3 is "the driving mode specific sustained performance by an ADS of all aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task within a given ODD with the expectation that the human driver will respond appropriately to a request to intervene," and its Automation Category is "Automated Driving System (ADS)." - Background context: driving automation technology "automates some or all aspects of the driving tasks to assist or replace the human driver and can include driver assistance technology generally known as advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS)." Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 5A-1, where Levels 1–2 are grouped under the "Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)" category while Levels 3–5 are grouped under "Automated Driving System (ADS)," visually confirming the categorical split at Level 3. [Image 4] shows page 760 with both the Section 5A.03 definition of ADS ("used specifically to describe a Level 3, 4, or 5 driving automation system") and Table 5A-1 immediately below it. Citations: - Section 5A.03 Support §1 (p.760) - Table 5A-1 (p.760) - Section 1C.03 Standard §1 (p.31) - Section 5A.02 Support §1 (p.759) - Page 800
gold_answer: An ADS performs the entire dynamic driving task on a sustained basis and the term applies to Levels 3-5. Level 2 performs steering and acceleration/deceleration but still expects the human to perform all remaining aspects of the task, so it is ADAS rather than ADS. Level 3 performs all aspects within its ODD, subject to a human fallback request.
